evidence: deepseek-v4-flash tests `if colors[nb] == c` before assigning the current vertex; gpt-oss-120b only checks `if nb < idx`; qwen3-coder explicitly attempts `all 3^n combinations` with constraint propagation, which conventionally checks only already-assigned neighbors
affordance_in_statement: “specific pairs of pillars are linked” and “a horizontal beam must never connect two pillars that share the exact same density rating”; the statement never explicitly says that u and v must be distinct or explains self-linked beams
removal_suggestion: Explicitly state in the scenario that a beam may have both endpoints on the same pillar (u=v is allowed), and that such a beam necessarily causes resonance because the pillar has the same rating at both ends. Keep the existing two-integer edge format and bounds.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Sequential backtracking checks neighbors while the current vertex is still unassigned, so a self-loop is never detected.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: “a horizontal beam must never connect two pillars that share the exact same density rating” without an explicit distinct-endpoint rule

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: The DFS deliberately checks only `nb < idx`, thereby ignoring a self-loop and all unassigned neighbors.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: “specific pairs of pillars are linked” does not explicitly exclude u=v

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: The advertised brute-force search with propagation follows the same assigned-neighbor assumption and will accept a self-loop unless it is checked after assignment.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The edge description does not define the behavior of a beam whose two endpoints are the same pillar

common_affordance: The implicit assumption that every beam connects two distinct pillars, allowing forward-checking solvers to ignore an edge from a vertex to itself

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its memoized state is `can_finish(remaining, forbidden)`, which compresses the per-vertex color restrictions into a single aggregate forbidden mask and cannot in general represent the coloring state of the remaining graph.

recommended_edit: Add: “A listed beam may connect a pillar to itself, so u=v is permitted. Such a self-beam is unsafe for every possible rating and therefore makes the answer NO.” Then include adversarial tests containing a self-loop.
